text:
Yaroslav Askarov is 4-8-0, and he has been good. That sentence says a lot about San Jose. Through 12 starts he has saved 4.36 goals above expected (saves beyond what the quality of shots predicts) on chances worth 44.36 expected goals, a heavy load for 12 starts. His high-danger save rate of 84% sits in the 75th percentile, and he ranks 12th of 75 goalies in our wins added, the measure of how much his saves moved his team's chances of winning.

This is a long way from last season, when he finished 19.4 goals below expected over 47 games. The pedigree always said this was possible: Nashville took him 11th overall in 2020, and Central Scouting had him as the top international goalie in that class.

Our talent estimate still sits near .880 to .890, so expect some of this to fade, and his last five starts have cooled to about even (0.51 above expected). We'd watch whether he can keep stealing points behind a defense that gives up this much, because the Sharks' climb runs through him.
headline: Askarov is the best thing about the Sharks' record
